video_title: Coinbase Launches Tokenized Stocks on Base
gist: Jesse Pollack (Base/Coinbase) details the mechanics, rollout, and strategic bet behind Coinbase's tokenized stocks on Base -- 1:1 backed, dividend-rebasing, DeFi-composable equities designed to turn Base into 'the exchange' of global finance, with Aerodrome/Morpho liquidity, a neo-bank-to-neo-brokerage thesis, and a parallel push to bring dozens of local-currency stablecoins on-chain.

insights.claim: Coinbase's tokenized stocks are structured as real 1:1-backed claims (not synthetic derivatives), built in partnership with Abu Dhabi (ADGM) and Alpaca, which Pollack argues will make them more trusted and adopted by both consumers and institutions than fragmented existing tokenized-equity products.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: 1:1 backing plus a regulated custody partner (ADGM) is the structural bet against fragmented, less-trusted tokenized-stock competitors -- watch for share of trading volume moving to Coinbase's product as a proof point.
insights.quote: every tokenized stock has a onetoone representation that users have a direct claim on

insights.claim: Dividends on Coinbase tokenized stocks are paid via a rebasing mechanism -- the token balance automatically increases by a multiplier when a dividend is issued -- rather than a separate cash payout, a deliberate design choice to make the tokens easier to use as DeFi collateral.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Rebasing avoids the collateral-accounting complexity of side-channel cash dividends, which is what makes these tokens usable in lending markets like Morpho -- a mechanism worth checking when evaluating any tokenized-equity product's DeFi composability.
insights.quote: there's a multiplier directly in the token so that ... you can show users, hey, you know, you just got this kind of increment that came in

insights.claim: The tokenized stocks carry full governance rights and dividend rights, positioned as 1:1 equivalent to holding the underlying US stock, not a stripped-down derivative.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Full governance/dividend parity is a differentiator investors should verify against competing tokenized-stock products, many of which strip these rights.

insights.claim: The tokens themselves are fully permissionless and require no KYC at the protocol/chain level -- restrictions on US persons are enforced only at the interface layer (apps, front-ends), not on-chain, meaning the tokens trade freely on Base DEXs like Aerodrome for anyone globally.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: This creates a durable channel for global (including technically US-adjacent) access regardless of any single front-end's geo-fencing -- relevant to both compliance risk assessment and to bullish liquidity/adoption modeling.
insights.quote: Freely permissionless, publicly available. Um, no KYC and they're uh they're restricted from US folks uh trading them at the interface layer.

insights.claim: Pollack expects price discovery for tokenized stocks to gradually migrate fully on-chain (rather than referencing the external US market) as Base liquidity deepens, citing Hyperliquid as an existing precedent for on-chain price-setting outside traditional market hours.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: If on-chain price discovery decouples from NYSE/Nasdaq hours, 24/7 tokenized equities could start trading at meaningfully different levels than the underlying during off-hours -- an arbitrage/mint-burn dynamic to monitor as adoption grows.
insights.quote: we're already kind of seeing this um with other venues like Hyperlid um and I expect that that's going to happen on base as well

insights.claim: The first four tokenized stocks launching are Nvidia, Meta, Apple, and Google, selected purely by observed retail demand, with eight more following within days and a stated goal of scaling to thousands of tokenized equities over time.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Retail-demand-led sequencing (mega-cap tech first) signals where initial liquidity and trading volume will concentrate -- useful for gauging early DeFi TVL contribution by name.
insights.quote: I think the first four that are rolling out are Nvidia, Meta, uh, Apple, and Google. And then we have another eight that are rolling out in the few days after that.

insights.claim: Minting and burning of tokenized stocks is initially restricted to a small, onboarded set of authorized liquidity providers, with the explicit long-term goal of letting any consumer who transfers real shares into Coinbase (or another brokerage) mint tokens directly and move them off-platform.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Watch for the mint/burn permission set to widen over time as a leading indicator of true self-custody adoption versus a still-gated, market-maker-dependent phase.

insights.claim: Base's DeFi TVL grew roughly 30-40% through the recent bear market over the last two years, a period in which most other crypto ecosystems saw declining TVL.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A counter-cyclical TVL grower during a bear market is a distinct relative-strength signal for Base versus peer L1/L2 ecosystems -- worth verifying against independent TVL trackers.
insights.quote: over the last two years, BAS is the the DeFi ecosystem that has grown through the bare market, I think we're up like something like 30 or 40%

insights.claim: Measured by 'financing' activity (lending, earning, borrowing products), Base has become the second-largest on-chain ecosystem in the world, having just overtaken Solana and trailing only Ethereum.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A claimed Solana flip in financing/lending activity is a specific, checkable competitive data point for anyone tracking L1/L2 market share in DeFi lending.
insights.quote: Base is now the second largest onchain ecosystem in the world after Ethereum. We just passed Salana.

insights.claim: Base's crypto-only DeFi has grown to roughly $5 billion, and Pollack states an explicit growth trajectory target of $10B, then $20B, then $50B, then $100B+ as tokenized real-world assets (starting with stocks) plug into that liquidity base.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A named, staged TVL growth target gives investors a concrete benchmark to track Base DeFi TVL against management's own stated milestones.

insights.claim: Aerodrome will provide the deepest day-one liquidity for the tokenized stocks and is designing new AMM structures specifically to handle equities that trade in concentrated volume windows (matching traditional market hours), addressing the LP-profitability problem this creates versus always-on crypto asset pools.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A novel AMM design for time-windowed-volume assets is a potential edge/product for Aerodrome LPs and a mechanism to watch for spillover into other RWA AMM design.

insights.claim: Morpho (and other lending protocols) will build borrowing/lending markets against the tokenized stocks, and because Base already aggregates deep USDC liquidity seeking yield, borrowers against these new stock collateral will get comparatively low borrowing rates, creating a liquidity flywheel.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Pre-existing idle USDC supply on Base is the funding source that could make Base's tokenized-equity borrow rates structurally cheaper than newer venues without that liquidity base -- a competitive moat argument to test.

insights.claim: Pollack frames tokenized stocks as roughly '6 months in,' compared to the ~4 years it took dollar stablecoins (USDC, Tether) to become a materially significant part of the crypto conversation, implicitly arguing tokenized equities are adopting faster on a comparable curve.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: This is a directly falsifiable claim (stablecoin adoption timeline vs. tokenized-stock adoption timeline) -- useful as a pacing benchmark for tracking whether tokenized-equity TVL/volume actually outpaces the stablecoin adoption curve.
insights.quote: it took four years for us to go from ... USDC and Tether issued to them really starting to be real material parts of the conversation. I think we're now like six months in with tokenized stocks essentially

insights.claim: Pollack explicitly rejects a pure liquidity-mining/incentive strategy to juice tokenized-stock trading volume, betting instead that usefulness -- portfolio-backed borrowing, covered-call yield generation, and business treasury use -- will drive durable adoption, even though the host notes the space is competitive with liquidity currently fragmented and no breakout winner.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A bet against short-term incentive-driven volume in favor of embedded utility is a thesis investors can test by watching whether Base's tokenized-stock volume retains stickiness without heavy token incentives, unlike prior tokenized-equity attempts.
insights.quote: I don't think that um just like raw incentives are trying to drive um like pure trading volume is is ultimately what's going to win here.

insights.claim: As an example of new treasury use cases, Pollack floats that an AI company heavily indexed to Nvidia products might choose to hold part of its corporate treasury directly in tokenized Nvidia stock once all assets sit on one interoperable financial platform.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Corporate treasury diversification into tokenized single-name equities (versus just stablecoins/BTC) would be a genuinely new corporate-treasury behavior worth watching for as an early real-world-asset adoption signal.
insights.quote: if you're an AI company and you're super indexed to uh Nvidia and you're using Nvidia products, like are you more likely to want to hold some of your treasury in Nvidia?

insights.claim: Business-banking partner Slash, which has already added stablecoins to its product because it operates wallet-like infrastructure behind the scenes, is cited as a natural near-term adopter of both Bitcoin and tokenized equities.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Slash is a concrete, named fintech to watch for near-term equity/BTC product additions as a signal of enterprise-side tokenized-stock adoption.

insights.claim: The Bankless host predicts 'neo-brokerage' will become the defining industry term of the remainder of 2026, echoing the earlier 'neo-bank' wave.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: A terminology call worth tracking as a sentiment/narrative indicator -- if 'neo-brokerage' fundraising and press mentions accelerate, it validates the framing as a genuine category shift rather than just marketing.
insights.quote: I do think the NEO brokerage word is going to be the word of the the rest of this year in 2026.

insights.claim: Neo-banks that have already piloted adding stock trading report better monetization than pure float/interest income, because they now capture trading revenue -- particularly strong in regions without deep integration into the US financial system where demand for US equities access is high.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Trading-fee monetization (not just float/interest spread) is emerging as a superior neo-bank revenue model in emerging markets -- a business-model shift relevant to evaluating fintech investments targeting non-US retail.
insights.quote: they're seeing that it's monetizing really well for them because now people are trading in their brokerage and they're not just monetizing float, they're actually monetizing trading

insights.claim: Pollack's framework: combining save, spend, invest, and borrow into a single crypto-rail-based product delivers outsized 'economic freedom' and is the core value proposition Base is building its enterprise sales motion around for neo-banks turning into neo-brokerages.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: The bundled save/spend/invest/borrow stack is Base's explicit enterprise pitch to fintechs -- a useful lens for evaluating which fintech partners are integrating Base versus building narrower single-feature products.
insights.quote: that whole combination of being able to save, spend, invest, and then borrow is just this huge huge unlock

insights.claim: The host's framing, which Pollack endorses: tokenization creates a de facto single 'global jurisdiction' covering everywhere outside the US, which is structurally simpler for a company to build compliant infrastructure for once than to replicate country-by-country banking-rail integrations.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: This reframes regulatory complexity as a one-time infrastructure/technology build rather than perpetual country-by-country legal replication -- a scalability argument for why crypto rails could out-execute traditional cross-border banking expansion.
insights.quote: the jurisdiction of tokenized stocks is everywhere. It's just the whole rest of the world.

insights.claim: Pollack argues the old model required getting a separate banking rail/bank account in every country to hold a local balance, which is why almost no banks span more than one jurisdiction; crypto instead offers one global stack reachable via a single API for trading, borrowing, lending, and payments everywhere.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: This is the structural argument for why crypto-native fintechs can out-scale traditional multinational banks -- a thesis for weighing crypto-rail-based neobanks against legacy cross-border banking incumbents.
insights.quote: why do we have so few banks that span more than one jurisdiction? It's because of that because it's so impossible.

insights.claim: Base currently has roughly 22-23 non-dollar local-currency stablecoins live (Pollack also separately states 'like 25 currencies' elsewhere in the conversation), with strongest adoption so far in Europe (EUR), Brazil, and Nigeria.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Note: Pollack cites inconsistent currency counts (22, 23, and 25) within the same interview -- treat the precise figure as approximate; directionally it signals early but real multi-currency stablecoin traction on Base.
insights.quote: I we're up to like 22 23 I think.

insights.claim: Total non-dollar stablecoin volume/size on Base is still small -- roughly $200 million -- indicating the multi-currency stablecoin push is real but early-stage relative to dollar stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable current-size figure for non-dollar stablecoins on Base -- useful as a baseline to track growth against Pollack's own ambition to scale from 22 to 100+ currencies.
insights.quote: there's something like $200 million of non-dollar stable coins on on base

insights.claim: Funding a neo-bank with dollars via a crypto on-ramp currently costs consumers roughly 1-2%, which Pollack calls not viable for most global consumers; the fix is local-currency stablecoin issuers who, like Circle/Coinbase do for USD, monetize the float to subsidize free 1:1 on-ramps in their own currency.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: This is an explicit 'call for startups': local-currency stablecoin issuance is framed as the unlock that lets neo-banks give away free on-ramps in non-dollar markets -- a concrete, underserved venture opportunity per Pollack.
insights.quote: you'd pay like 1% or 2% to fund a neo bank. That's like not really uh viable for most consumers.

insights.claim: Pollack predicts that over the next decade Nigeria (and similarly Argentina, Brazil, Turkey) will come on-chain denominated in their own sovereign currency rather than the dollar, because countries will not fully cede their currencies, and argues this is a large open opportunity for local builders.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A specific, testable multi-year prediction about local-currency (not dollar) denominated on-chain adoption in major EM crypto markets -- relevant for anyone evaluating stablecoin-issuer or local-DeFi startups in Nigeria, Argentina, Brazil, or Turkey.
insights.quote: over the next decade Nigeria will come on chain and it will be denominated in Naira

insights.claim: Coinbase/Base is actively building portfolio-backed credit-line infrastructure so users can hold a mixed portfolio of stablecoins and tokenized equities and borrow roughly 30-40% against it out of the box -- described as a needed 'stitching together' piece that isn't fully live yet.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Portfolio-margin-style borrowing across mixed crypto/equity collateral is a concrete near-term product to watch launch, since Pollack names it as an active current build rather than a shipped feature.
insights.quote: how do we also give you um uh like a portfolio line of credit infrastructure so you can have all of those assets sit in your portfolio and then you can borrow 30% against it or 40% against it

insights.claim: Jesse Pollack has narrowed his role to focus purely on chain-building at Base (product/engineering roadmap, go-to-market, BD, community) and handed off leadership of the consumer-facing Base App to 'Kobe,' who joined Coinbase via its acquisition of Echo roughly 9-12 months earlier.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: An internal leadership restructuring signals Coinbase is treating the Base chain and the Base consumer trading app as increasingly distinct, professionalized business lines -- relevant to tracking accountability for Base's roadmap versus its trading-app growth.
insights.quote: luckily uh nine months ago, a year ago, I championed uh the the acquisition of Ekko and bringing Kobe into Coinbase

insights.claim: Kobe now leads trading strategy across the entire Coinbase consumer app, the Base App, and the tokenization effort that bridges off-chain equities onto Base -- consolidating trading leadership under one person across all of Coinbase's surfaces.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: A single leader owning trading strategy across Coinbase.com, the Base App, and tokenization suggests tighter coordination and potentially faster cross-surface rollout of tokenized-stock features.
insights.quote: he has now been leading actually the tokenized stocks work

insights.claim: Base is shipping native account abstraction in its next release, along with stablecoin-denominated gas payments and improved token standards, running on Base's own independent technology stack rather than shared Ethereum L2 tooling.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Concrete near-term protocol upgrades (account abstraction, stablecoin gas) to watch ship on Base, and evidence Base is increasingly differentiating its own stack rather than following a shared L2 roadmap.
insights.quote: we're shipping native account abstraction in the next release

insights.claim: Positioning framework: Base is explicitly building to be 'the exchange' -- covering trading, financing, and payments -- as the complementary counterpart to Ethereum's role as the 'world computer,' referencing a Vitalik Buterin tweet stating Ethereum isn't primarily for trading.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: This is Coinbase's explicit strategic positioning of Base versus Ethereum L1 and other L2s -- a clean thesis to test against where trading/DeFi volume actually concentrates over time.
insights.quote: Ethereum isn't just for trading. base is for trading.

insights.claim: Base continues to pay Ethereum daily for blob space and says it wants more blob space capacity as demand grows, explicitly framing itself as a 'happy Ethereum customer' rather than a competitor to L1 settlement.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Confirms Base's continued economic dependency on and alignment with Ethereum blob-space fee revenue, relevant to modeling Ethereum's data-availability fee demand as L2 activity (especially RWA trading) scales.
insights.quote: we're a happy Ethereum customer um paying for blob space every single day

insights.claim: Coinbase intends to expand tokenized stocks to blockchain networks beyond Base over time, with Base positioned as the central hub rather than an exclusive venue, though Pollack declines to give specific timelines or name other target chains.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock
insights.so_what: Multi-chain expansion of Coinbase's tokenized-stock product would dilute any Base-exclusivity liquidity moat -- worth monitoring for announcements of tokenized stocks appearing on other chains (e.g., a potential move onto Ethereum mainnet).
insights.quote: I think that Coinbase is going to bring tokenized stocks to more places than just base.
